request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to people and claims on a sheet is now written to the audit file, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. I only changed the server; the screens didn't need anything new.

- **Lines written:** adding or editing a person writes `PERSON_ADDED` or `PERSON_EDITED` with the name and grade. Adding or editing a claim writes `CLAIM_ADDED` or `CLAIM_EDITED` with the person's name, the amount with two decimals and the date as yyyy-mm-dd. Each line starts with the event, then `sheet=` and `by=`, where `by=` is the signed-in user.
- **Refused changes write nothing:** a line is only written once the change has been saved for good. The change is saved before the line is queued, so if a rule refuses it or the save fails, no line appears. This covers rules added later too, as long as they run inside the same service call. I added a `recordOnCommit` method to `Audit.java` for this.
- **Where the code is:** the lines are built in `PersonService` and `ClaimService`. The controllers now pass the signed-in user through to them.

Two behaviours you might not expect, both required by the tests:
- An edit that leaves the values the same still writes a line, for example setting Ada's grade to B when it's already B.
- A claim line uses the person's name as it is at that moment, so if someone is renamed, newer lines show the new name.
